page: Microsoft Azure D48as_v6 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the Dav6 server family. It is powered by an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture, operating at a clock speed of 3.7 GHz. The instance features 48 dedicated vCPUs derived from 24 physical cores with multithreading enabled. It is equipped with 192.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced allocation of 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. This server does not include local storage or onboard GPUs, but it is Premium Storage capable, allowing high-performance external disk attachments.

In benchmark evaluations, the D48as_v6 demonstrates strong performance, particularly in CPU-bound and memory-intensive operations. It achieves top-25% scores in stress-ng single-core and multi-core tests, as well as Geekbench single-core and multi-core evaluations. Cryptographic and vector processing capabilities are enhanced by hardware support for AVX-512 and AES instructions, reflected in strong Passmark CPU encryption and extended instruction scores. Memory performance is robust, with small-block cached read bandwidth reaching 3648.65 GB/sec, though large-block uncached read and write bandwidths fall into the average tier.

The server is highly capable for multi-threaded decompression, software compilation, and Redis key-value operations, where it processes 66.46 million SET operations per second. For artificial intelligence workloads, it delivers top-tier text generation speeds of 340.72 tokens/sec on small 135M models, but performance drops to average or weak tiers when processing medium and large LLM models due to the lack of dedicated GPU acceleration. This hardware profile is well-suited for general-purpose enterprise workloads, multi-threaded data processing, software development pipelines, and web serving, offering a balanced resource density without the overhead of local storage.
